DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION
1. General
The passenger seats are arranged into two rows in the aircraft, one comprising single seats and
another comprising double seats. In some configurations, the last row may also comprise triple
seats.
2. Description
A. The Single Passenger Seat (Figure 1) configurations listed below may be found on the "EMB-
120" Brasilia:
(1) First row single passenger seat with plug-in type snack table.
(2) Complete Single Passenger Seat with two armrests and snack folding table.
(3) Single Passenger Seat without armrest on the wall side (emergency exit position).
(4) Single Passenger Seat without snack folding table (last row).
(5) Single Passenger Seat with longer armrest, without snack folding table, to fit the triple pas-
senger seat row.
B. The Double Passenger Seat (Figure 2) may be found in the following configurations:

ILLUSTRATED PARTS LIST
1. General
A. This section lists and illustrates all the applicable assemblies, subassemblies, and components.
2. Vendor's List
A. A list of names and addresses of vendors is supplied together with the relevant codes for refer-
ence in the Detailed Parts List. The list is arranged in numerical order, according to the vendor
codes. Vendor part numbers with no FEDERAL SUPPLY CODE or NATO SUPPLY CODE
assigned are therein identified with a code preceded by the capital letter "E".
3. Numerical Index
A. The numerical index contains every number that appears in the Detailed Parts List and is
arranged in dual columns, in alphanumerical sequence.
(1) PART NUMBER Column.
The part number starts at the extreme left hand, continuing to the right, one position at a
time.
The order of precedence due to the part number arrangement for the first position (extreme
left) is the following:
- Letters A thru Z
- Numerals 0 thru
